thread:
jo: Heads-up: hit a reproducible dup-write bug in the Kotlin sample uploader on Pixel emulator (API 34). Using Retrofit + OkHttp with a streaming RequestBody and our TokenAuthenticator -> occasionally the server receives the same PATCH twice.
rachel: did you confirm it's the client re-sending and not our backend retrying?
jo: yes; server logs show two identical PATCH bodies and same client IP/conn id. Client logs show a socket reset followed by token refresh and then a second send.
tony: streaming bodies are non-repeatable by default. If OkHttp retries a call after failure (or an Authenticator triggers a retry), it may re-send the request, causing duplicate side-effects.
jo: simplified repro steps I used:
- run sample on emulator
- trigger one large streaming PATCH with chunked RequestBody
- drop connection mid-upload (simulate reset)
- Authenticator runs and triggers a refresh -> request gets retried -> server sees second complete PATCH
rachel: can you paste the RequestBody impl?
jo: trimmed:
```
class StreamRequestBody(val src: InputStream) : RequestBody() {
  override fun contentType() = "application/json".toMediaTypeOrNull()
  override fun writeTo(sink: BufferedSink) {
    src.source().use { it.readAll(sink) }
  }
}
```
tony: yep non-repeatable. Workarounds we discussed: 1) buffer to file/byte array to make a repeatable RequestBody, 2) disable retryOnConnectionFailure for clients that send non-repeatable bodies, 3) add idempotency-key header server-side, 4) ensure auth refresh uses a separate OkHttpClient to avoid dispatcher deadlock.
jo: I tried disabling retryOnConnectionFailure on the uploader client and that removed duplicate sends in the repro.
rachel: related note: Authenticator should not make blocking calls on the same client — that can starve dispatcher threads and lead to weird retries. Use a dedicated client for auth refresh.
tony: example snippet for dedicated auth client:
```
val authClient = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 1 })
  .build()
val authRetrofit = Retrofit.Builder().client(authClient)...
```
jo: filed a tiny repro in our sample repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kotlin-sdk-repros/pull/72 — includes an emulator test toggling retryOnConnectionFailure and a small server that records duplicate bodies.
ci-bot: CI run 912 for branch fix-stream-dup completed: https://ci.redwood.dev/build/912 :white_check_mark:
rachel: can we add a short guidance blurb in docs: "When sending non-repeatable RequestBody from Android clients: either make bodies repeatable, disable connection retries, use idempotency keys, and ensure auth refresh is on a separate client."
jo: agreed — I'll open a docs PR and attach the minimal repro. Thanks all. :pray:
